title: Where it grows
subtitle: Italy and France
objectives: Explain its role in French brandy

steps.title: Italy
steps.body: Trebbiano grows across central Italy. Trebbiano Toscano is used in Tuscany, Umbria and Lazio, often in blends like Orvieto and Frascati, and in Vin Santo. Trebbiano Romagnolo grows in Emilia-Romagna. Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is a separate variety. Lugana, near Lake Garda, uses Turbiana, once called Trebbiano di Lugana.

steps.title: France
steps.body: In France, Ugni Blanc is the main grape of Cognac, about 98% of plantings there, and Armagnac. In the south, it's used in Côtes de Gascogne IGP whites, often blended with Colombard. Local names include Saint-Émilion in Charente, unrelated to the Bordeaux village.

steps.prompt: Match each name to its place.
steps.explanation: The Trebbiano family has many members.

steps.body: In Cognac, Ugni Blanc's local name is Saint-Émilion. Don't confuse it with the Bordeaux appellation.

steps.prompt: Which wines or spirits use Trebbiano or Ugni Blanc?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Trebbiano grows across central Italy in several varieties
Ugni Blanc is about 98% of Cognac
It's used in Gascony whites and Armagnac
